summary.headline: Cheap against its assets, but those assets earn little for Renuka's own shareholders
summary.text: Renuka Holdings (RHL.N0000 voting, RHL.X0000 non-voting) is a family-controlled holding company. It owns 43% of Renuka Foods (Richlife dairy, Shaw Wallace FMCG and, through it, 20% of Renuka Agri Foods' coconut exports), 44% of Ceylon Land & Equity (owner of the unfinished Galle Face Icon tower site in Colombo 3), a share portfolio and Colombo land. Its book value is about Rs 50 a share, and its stakes in listed subsidiaries are worth about Rs 42–46 a share at today's market prices, so at Rs 36.90 (CSE, 11 November 2026) the voting share looks cheap on assets. But that value earns little for Renuka's own shareholders: their return on equity has been 7% or less every year (a loss in 2023/24), about 70% of last year's Rs 702m profit came from the property and investment arm, mostly share-portfolio gains, and dividends are tiny and paid in new shares (Rs 0.212 for 2025/26). During the year the group sold down stakes in its subsidiaries below book value, which cut owners' equity by Rs 684m, and the auditors' adjustments cut the year's profit by 31% from the March interim. With a 18% required return, four methods put fair value at about Rs 26.80, so the voting share is about 38% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 22.80 and treat under Rs 20.10 as a strong buy. The non-voting share (Rs 26.00, same dividends and earnings) is at about fair value and is the better way in if you want exposure; it traded as low as Rs 22.50 this year.

quality.reason: Net cash, but low returns for owners, a loss three years ago, profit reliant on share-portfolio gains, and weak cash flow with only scrip dividends.

highlights.title: 2025/26 (audited)
highlights.text: Revenue up 30% to Rs 18.2bn as coconut exports rose to Rs 9.75bn from Rs 6.27bn; gross profit Rs 3.4bn (Rs 1.9bn). Group profit Rs 1.25bn (Rs 0.31bn), of which Rs 702m to Renuka's shareholders (EPS Rs 3.70 against Rs 0.36). Property and investment earned Rs 714m, helped by Rs 747m of share-portfolio gains as the CSE rallied.

highlights.title: Big audit adjustments
highlights.text: The unaudited March interim showed owners' profit of Rs 1,014m (EPS Rs 5.34) and NAV Rs 56.86; the audited figures are Rs 702m (EPS Rs 3.70) and Rs 50.93, mainly lower fair-value gains and Rs 533m more tax, mostly deferred. The December interim had to be reissued with errata, and the June interim still starts from an unaudited March balance sheet (owners' equity Rs 10.08bn instead of the audited Rs 9.66bn).

highlights.title: Stakes sold down; minorities now own most of the group
highlights.text: Ceylon Land & Equity raised Rs 4.3bn in a rights issue for the Galle Face project, and the group sold shares in Renuka Foods, Renuka Agri Foods and Galle Face Capital Partners. Renuka's effective stake in Renuka Agri Foods fell from 43% to 20% and in Renuka Foods from 57% to 43%. The deals were done below book value, cutting owners' equity by Rs 684m, and minority interests rose to Rs 11.6bn (54% of group equity).

highlights.title: April–June 2026 quarter (unaudited)
highlights.text: Revenue flat at Rs 3.85bn; gross margin up to 20.6% (17.2%). Group profit Rs 407m (Rs 427m), owners' share Rs 148m (EPS Rs 0.78 against Rs 1.09). Interest income jumped to Rs 293m on the rights-issue cash, while share-portfolio gains fell to Rs 14m from Rs 306m. Agri exports swung to a Rs 125m profit; consumer brands fell to Rs 29m.

highlights.title: Scrip dividend and auditor change
highlights.text: A first and final dividend of Rs 0.212 a share for 2025/26 was paid in new shares (788,393 voting and 160,336 non-voting). Shareholders were asked to appoint Ernst & Young as auditors from 2026/27, replacing KPMG.

The non-voting share is already near fair value (Rs 26.00) and traded down to Rs 22.50 this year, so the buy price is realistic for it. notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2024/25 and 2025/26 annual reports and the interim reports to June 2026 (unaudited and not reviewed). The September 2026 quarter wasn't in the folder. Look-through values use CSE prices of 11 November 2026. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: the voting share is about 38% above fair value of Rs 26.80; the non-voting share (Rs 26.00) is at about fair value.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 36.90: About −4% a year over three years: dividend 0.6% + book growth about 5% − about 10% a year if the price moved to fair value. The non-voting share at Rs 26.00 would earn about 7% a year, still below the T-bill.
Decision box.Downside / upside: Bear case −43% (Rs 20.90); bull case −7% (Rs 34.50). Against the non-voting price: bear −20%, bull +33%.
Decision box.What the price assumes: A holding-company discount of only about 26% to NAV and 16% to the listed stakes, or owners' ROE of about 14%, double anything the group has earned in five years.
Decision box.Confidence: Low: the methods give Rs 20–33 in the base case; audit adjustments were large, and owners' earnings depend on share-market gains.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Buy 15% below fair value (Rs 22.80), strong buy 25% below (Rs 20.10).

Business and moat.What it does: A holding company in three sectors: agri food exports (Renuka Agri Foods: coconut milk, cream and other coconut products, mostly to Europe; 56% of 2025/26 revenue), consumer brands (Renuka Foods: Richlife dairy, Shaw Wallace fish, soya, snacks and juices; 44%), and property and investment (Ceylon Land & Equity, Galle Face Capital Partners, Colombo land, a share portfolio).
Business and moat.Segment profit 2025/26: Agri exports Rs 146m (a Rs 733m loss in 2024/25), consumer brands Rs 387m (Rs 488m), property and investment Rs 714m (Rs 551m), all before minority interests.
Business and moat.Moat: Narrow: established export customers and private-label contracts in coconut products, Richlife's dairy brand and Shaw Wallace's distribution to 70,000 outlets. Coconut exports depend on volatile raw-coconut prices.
Business and moat.Growth drivers: Coconut milk in Tetra packs (+38%), bulk and private-label exports to Europe, dairy's wider retail reach (25,000 → 35,000 outlets), and the Galle Face land.
Business and moat.Holding structure: Renuka owns 72% of Renuka Investments, which holds most of the group; effective stakes: Renuka Foods 43%, Ceylon Land & Equity 44%, Renuka Agri Foods 20%, Galle Face Properties 65%, Galle Face Capital Partners 30%. Minority shareholders own 54% of group equity.

Management and governance.Ownership: The Rajiyah family controls it: Renuka Group Ltd 50.07% of voting shares (up from 46.89% in March) plus two family joint holdings of 10.03% each. Public float 29.61% of voting and 93.03% of non-voting shares.
Management and governance.Track record: Grew exports and raised Rs 4.3bn for the Galle Face project, but owners' returns have stayed in single digits, and the group sold subsidiary stakes below book value (−Rs 684m to owners).
Management and governance.Pay and related parties: Key management pay Rs 340m in 2025/26 (Rs 169m in 2024/25), about half of owners' profit. Royalty of Rs 89m paid to Renuka International Ltd and Rs 14.4m rent to Renuka Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, both director-linked.
Management and governance.Capital allocation: Dividends paid in new shares; cash raised mostly sits in subsidiaries. The Galle Face Icon (30 storeys, started in 2018) is still unfinished, and its capital commitments are 'under renegotiation'.
Management and governance.Auditor: KPMG, clean opinion for 2025/26; key audit matters included revenue recognition, investment in subsidiaries, receivables and inventories. Ernst & Young proposed from 2026/27.
Management and governance.Directors: The chairperson (75) and deputy chairman (76) were re-appointed above the age limit by special resolution.

Accounting quality.Audit adjustments: Audited 2025/26 owners' profit was Rs 702m against Rs 1,014m in the March interim, and group profit Rs 1.25bn against Rs 2.63bn, mainly lower fair-value gains and Rs 533m more tax, mostly deferred.
Accounting quality.Interim reliability: The December 2025 interim was reissued (errata changed quarterly owners' profit from Rs 38m to Rs 117m). The June 2026 interim's opening balance is the unaudited March figure, so its NAV of Rs 52.57 is about Rs 2.20 too high.
Accounting quality.Underlying earnings: About Rs 870m of the year's pre-tax profit came from share-portfolio gains and other financial items; the food businesses earned about Rs 200m for Renuka's owners.
Accounting quality.Revaluations: Land and buildings are revalued; investment property (Rs 5.8bn) includes Rs 2.2bn of building work in progress on the Galle Face Icon, which has no independent valuation.
Accounting quality.Inventory: Rs 122m provision for obsolete stock in 2025/26 (a Rs 42m release the year before).

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: policy rate 8.75%, 10-year bond about 12.4%. The group earns interest on Rs 6bn of cash but borrows Rs 3.6bn short term.
Sri Lanka checks.Rupee and exports: Watch: 35–54% of revenue is exports (EUR/USD), so a weaker rupee helps exports; raw-coconut prices are the main cost risk.
Sri Lanka checks.Trade: Risk: US tariffs on Sri Lankan exports and the EU Deforestation Regulation affect the coconut business.
Sri Lanka checks.Share-market exposure: Risk: Rs 3.3bn of quoted shares (Cargills, Aitken Spence and others) drive profit swings.
Sri Lanka checks.Property: Watch: the Galle Face land (Rs 2.2bn) and unfinished tower depend on Colombo's office and apartment market.
Sri Lanka checks.Liquidity: Thin: about 5,400 voting trades a year; non-voting much less. 500 shares are possible with patience.
Sri Lanka checks.Free float and control: Family-controlled through Renuka Group Ltd; minority shareholders have little influence.
Sri Lanka checks.Catalysts: September 2026 quarter results (due by mid-November), the Galle Face project plan, first year with the new auditors.

Crisis stress test (2022-style).Scenario: Share market falls 40%, interest rates up 10 points, coconut costs spike.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Likely effect (rough estimate): Portfolio loss about Rs 1.3bn (Renuka's share roughly Rs 0.6bn, Rs 3 a share); export margins squeezed as in 2023/24 (a group loss). Net cash cushions the rate rise.
Crisis stress test (2022-style).Survival: Survives: net cash and no holding-company debt. NAV might fall to about Rs 44–46 and the share would likely trade at a 50%+ discount.

Portfolio fit.Cost of 500 shares: About Rs 18,450 (voting) or Rs 13,000 (non-voting) now; about Rs 11,400 at the buy price.
Portfolio fit.Overlap: None with other companies on the site; its food and coconut exposure is new.
Portfolio fit.Note: Shown for information, not as advice on how much to hold.

Broker view.Coverage: No broker view in the summaries collected so far.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: Only as a discounted asset play: buying Rs 50 of book value for well under half, with net cash and a food business that recovered in 2025/26.
Investment case and sell rules.The case is broken if: More value is moved from Renuka's shareholders to minorities or related parties, or the Galle Face project needs large new funding.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 34.80: the voting share is above this); the case breaks; or a clearly better opportunity appears.

Suggested Telegram alerts (not set; need.Sell trigger: Rs 34.80 or higher (voting share already above)

Key ratios (five-year trend).Net debt: Mar 2025 Rs 3.8bn · Mar 2026 net cash Rs 2.3bn · Jun 2026 net cash Rs 2.0bn
Key ratios (five-year trend).Graham number: Rs 61.80 (√(22.5 × EPS 3.39 × NAV 50.12)); overstates value because the EPS is mostly portfolio gains

What this analysis doesn't cover: The September 2026 quarter (not yet in the folder).

fullText:
Summary: Renuka Holdings (RHL.N0000 voting, RHL.X0000 non-voting) is a family-controlled holding company. It owns 43% of Renuka Foods (Richlife dairy, Shaw Wallace FMCG and, through it, 20% of Renuka Agri Foods' coconut exports), 44% of Ceylon Land & Equity (owner of the unfinished Galle Face Icon tower site in Colombo 3), a share portfolio and Colombo land. Its book value is about Rs 50 a share, and its stakes in listed subsidiaries are worth about Rs 42–46 a share at today's market prices, so at Rs 36.90 (CSE, 11 November 2026) the voting share looks cheap on assets. But that value earns little for Renuka's own shareholders: their return on equity has been 7% or less every year (a loss in 2023/24), about 70% of last year's Rs 702m profit came from the property and investment arm, mostly share-portfolio gains, and dividends are tiny and paid in new shares (Rs 0.212 for 2025/26). During the year the group sold down stakes in its subsidiaries below book value, which cut owners' equity by Rs 684m, and the auditors' adjustments cut the year's profit by 31% from the March interim. With a 18% required return, four methods put fair value at about Rs 26.80, so the voting share is about 38% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 22.80 and treat under Rs 20.10 as a strong buy. The non-voting share (Rs 26.00, same dividends and earnings) is at about fair value and is the better way in if you want exposure; it traded as low as Rs 22.50 this year.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 36.90 voting, Rs 26.00 non-voting (CSE, 11 November 2026). 12-month range: voting Rs 31.80–64.90, non-voting Rs 22.50–46.30. The voting share closed March 2026 at Rs 50.70 and March 2025 at Rs 18.00.
2025/26 (audited): revenue Rs 18.2bn (up 30%), gross profit Rs 3.4bn, group profit Rs 1.25bn, owners' profit Rs 702m, EPS Rs 3.70, owners' ROE 7.3%, NAV Rs 50.93.
April–June 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 3.85bn, group profit Rs 407m, owners' profit Rs 148m, EPS Rs 0.78 (Rs 1.09). Net cash about Rs 2.0bn. NAV about Rs 50.12 (rebuilt from the audited March figure; the company reports Rs 52.57).
Listed stakes at 11 November prices: Renuka Foods Rs 3.7bn, Ceylon Land & Equity Rs 3.6bn, Galle Face Capital Partners Rs 0.8bn, plus Campbell Place land Rs 0.7bn: about Rs 42–46 a share.

Decision box
Fair value about Rs 26.80. The voting share is about 38% above it; the non-voting share is about at it. Expected return at Rs 36.90 about −4% a year over three years, against a one-year T-bill of about 9.1%. Bear case −43%, bull case −7% (voting). Confidence low, so I rely on deep discounts: buy up to Rs 22.80, strong buy under Rs 20.10.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
NAV less discount | 27.6 | 32.6 | 37.6 | 32.1
Sum of the parts | 25.1 | 30.7 | 36.6 | 30.2
P/E | 16.0 | 26.0 | 38.4 | 25.5
Residual income | 14.9 | 19.6 | 25.5 | 19.4
Average | 20.9 | 27.2 | 34.5 | 26.8

Assumptions
Cost of equity 19% / 18% / 17% (bond about 12.4% plus 5.5 points for a small, family-controlled holding company). Holding-company discount 45% / 35% / 25% to NAV and 40% / 30% / 20% to listed stakes at market. Normal EPS Rs 2.00 / 2.60 / 3.20 at 8 / 10 / 12 times. Owners' ROE 5% / 7% / 9%.

Why the asset value isn't the answer
Book value is about Rs 50 a share, but Renuka's owners have earned 7% or less on it every year, about 70% of last year's profit came from share-portfolio gains, cash flow has been weak, and dividends are paid in shares. During 2025/26 the group sold subsidiary stakes below book value (−Rs 684m to owners), and minorities now own 54% of group equity. Holding companies like this usually trade 30–50% below their assets on the CSE.

Accounting quality
The auditors cut the year's owners' profit from Rs 1,014m (March interim) to Rs 702m, the December interim was reissued, and the June interim starts from an unaudited balance sheet. Key management pay doubled to Rs 340m. The new auditors (Ernst & Young, from 2026/27) are worth watching.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (debt: net cash; fails returns, steady profit and cash conversion), so it's a weak business: avoid for now. The non-voting share near Rs 22.80 would be a reasonable asset play for patient investors.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 26.80, 150 up to Rs 22.80, 150 up to Rs 20.10 (either class): average about Rs 23.60, about Rs 11,800 in total. The non-voting share is already near the first tier and traded at Rs 22.50 this year; the voting share would need a 38% fall to reach Rs 22.80.

Sell rules
If you already hold the voting share: it is above the sell trigger (30% above fair value, Rs 34.80).
